idiom_name: hand-written state-holder struct with Rc<RefCell<T>>/Cell and Drop for cleanup
implementation_notes: Rust has no host runtime and no ambient state slots, so the unit is a hand-written type: a struct owns the state and exposes methods, shared mutation goes through the documented interior-mutability tools (Cell for Copy values, RefCell for the rest, Rc when several owners need the same value), and a Drop implementation is Rust's replacement for effect teardown. Closures capturing the handle can act as the returned action surface - fn counter() -> (Rc<Cell<i32>>, impl FnMut()) mirrors a hook's state/action pair - but without a render lifecycle there are no keys, dependency arrays or ordering rules, and callers compose by owning the handle. Interior mutability is the escape hatch for aliasing plus mutation rather than the default: prefer owned data and &mut self methods, reach for Rc<RefCell<_>> only where a host would have provided slots, and use Arc<Mutex<_>> across threads because Cell and RefCell are not Sync.
pitfalls: RefCell enforces the borrow rules at runtime: a second borrow_mut while a borrow is live panics, so keep borrows short and never hold a guard across a callback.
Rc cycles leak because reference counts never reach zero; use Weak for back-references when the unit stores handles back to its consumers.
Cell and RefCell are not Sync, so sharing the unit across threads requires Arc<Mutex<_>>/Arc<RwLock<_>> or moving ownership through channels.
